newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico central bank sees longer-term domestic debt.
newsitem.headline: Mexico central bank sees longer-term domestic debt.

text.p: Mexico may issue longer-term peso-denominated debt, Banco de Mexico General Director of Economic Research Agustin Carstens said on Thursday.
He spoke in a conference call with analysts to explain the central bank's 1997 monetary policy plan.

In response to a question on whether Mexico might issue longer-term Cetes, or treasury bills, Carstens said that, "Certainly we expect that during this year (1997) longer-term instruments in Mexico will be issued."
At present, the longest term Cetes are for one-year.
Private pension funds, or AFORES, are scheduled to start working in the second half of 1997, and that will spur the development of a peso-denominated debt market, he said.

"The new pension fund reforms, when they start working in the second half of the year, would lend themselves not only for public sector debt to increase maturity, but will also be a very good opportunity for long-term private sector debt to be started to be issued here in Mexico," Carstens said.
He said the new instruments would also likely have to have credit ratings.
"Certainly we will introduce some requirements for ratings and so on to keep an eye on the credit risk of these instruments," he said.
